d.g: A form of rusk, usually sweetened bread enriched with eggs that is baked and then sliced and toasted until dry and crisp; considered easy to digest and therefore given to the ill and used as a teething food for toddlers.
d.x:
Ogden Nash, Adventures Of Isabel
She nibbled the zwieback that she always fed off,
And when it was gone, she cut the giant's head off.

zwieback.e: From German Zwieback, from zwie- (“twi-, two-”) + backen (“to bake”) (i.e. “twice-baked”), a calque of Italian biscotto (but not to be confused with it).

d.g: Swiss theologian whose sermons began the Reformation in Switzerland (1484-1531)
United States physicist who invented the iconoscope (1889-1982)
